utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-8-PT, the Prosecutor versus Damir Dosen and Dragan Kolundzija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think you had the microphone on. Well, all right, it doesn't matter. May we have the appearances, please? Could we have the appearances, please. [In English] We are late, and I hope it will be repaired soon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you would introduce yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Brenda Hollis, Kapila Waidyaratne, and Dan Saxon appear on behalf of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Judge. Dusan Vucicevic from Chicago, Illinois, on behalf of Dragan Kolundzija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Vladimir Petrovic, attorney at law from Zagreb. Together with Sanja Turlokov, I appear for Damir Dosen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Petrovic. I would like to ensure that the accused, Mr. Kolundzija and Mr. Dosen, are following the proceedings in this courtroom in a language they understand. [In English] No translation. [Interpretation] Yes, that was the purpose of my question. They are not getting the interpretation. Can the accused, Mr. Kolundzija and Mr. Dosen, hear me? Are you following the proceedings in a language which you understand? Mr. Dosen as well? Thank you. This Status Conference, as you probably know, will deal with three points that I'm going to announce at the beginning, although I do regret the delay and so we'll try to focus on the most important points, because this is a status conference which is important. The three points are the following: Let me remind you briefly of the issues that are pending before this Chamber and which will be the subject of a hearing which was most likely announced to you already and which will take place on the 23rd of June at 11 o’clock, the 23rd of June at 11 o’clock, because the Chamber is -- or at least two of the Judges are involved in another case before 11 o’clock. After that, we will discuss the issue of the opening of the trial, this trial. The third point is any additional time requested by the Prosecutor for the presentation of the pre-trial brief and the list of witnesses. And after that we will discuss the preparations for the trial, in general terms, and the calendar which is needed for -- the calendar we've got to set in order to prepare for this trial. Then, of course, any other questions at the end. The first point is simply a reminder that I'm going to make for the Prosecutor and for the Defence in respect of the pending questions which will be dealt with during the hearing which will take place on the 23rd of June. What I have just said, moreover, in part will depend on the request which was submitted to us by the Defence, that Mr. Vucicevic sent to us dated 6 June, and which is called: [In English] "The Defence request for oral argument on pending motions before Judge Trial Chamber III." [Interpretation] We received that from Mr. Vucicevic, and we received it on the 6th of June. What points are going to be taken up on the 23rd of June? First of all is the issue of the amended attachment, attachment to the indictment, and the parties will be heard during that hearing. Let me remind you that the problem of the Prosecutor's presentation of a single document -- a consolidated, unique, or single indictment remains an issue, and this is going to have to be done before the trial begins, of course, so that we can have not the two indictments which we have today, but a single indictment which has been consolidated. This is a reminder. The second point which will be taken up on the 23rd of June is the request for judicial notice, and then the third part will be the request for the admission of documents, about which there were written submissions including the answer or the reply which I authorised, and we can speak -- you can speak before the Chamber on the 23rd of June. And then there is the motion for the accused Kolundzija [previous translation continues]... [In English] counts and/or for bifurcation of trial. [Interpretation] We received the Prosecutor's response on the 5th of June, as was planned, and these are the points which I'm reminding you of and which will be on the agenda for the hearing scheduled for the 23rd of June. A final point which I would like to recall here is the one which has to do with the request for protective measures of the 12 witnesses, which was presented to us by the Prosecutor on the 1st of June. This request for protective measures relates to the disclosure of non-redacted excerpts which were ordered by the Trial Chamber on the 11th of May. I would now like to turn to you, Mr. Vucicevic and you Mr. Petrovic and ask you whether you intend to respond in writing to this request within the time period which runs until the 15th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot affirmatively answer that, I will -- because I am planning to travel to Bosnia to do some investigation and I was planning on 23rd to be -- actually 24th to be flying back to Chicago so I will be away from my office, but I will do my best to review the document. I didn't get a chance to review it fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. My question is whether you intend to respond in writing to the Prosecutor's request or do you not intend to respond in writing or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I haven't reviewed it, Your Honour, yet in detail because -- and I can't give you an answer because if I would -- for practicality's sake, I would tell you that I would respond in writing to preserve my right to respond in writing. And if I decide that the response will not be necessary, I will just, you know, submit you a notice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence for the accused, Dosen, will respond in writing within the time period that is envisaged that is to say 15 days upon receipt of the brief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have been informed that you have until the 15th of June to respond in writing because as you've just been reminded, Mr. Petrovic, that's the deadline for the -- that runs -- it starts on the 1st of June. The decision will be issued by myself as the pre-trial Judge after the 15th of June. As regards that hearing on the 23rd of June, I'm turning to the Prosecutor as well as the Defence. Do you have any questions you'd like to ask so that I could move to the second point on the agenda for this Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour I don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vucicevic. Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour regarding the hearing that you just announced, we don't anticipate any difficulties with that date and time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Dosen Defence has no particular questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As regards the second point that we've got to take up today during this Status Conference is the date for the start of the trial. The Chamber has, of course, paid a great deal of attention to this question and has kept in mind that the trial must be a fair one and take place as quickly as possible as provided for in the Statute. Depending on, of course, the very busy schedule of the Chamber and of our other commitments. So we agreed that one of the possible dates could be the 6th of November this year. This is one of the possible dates for the start of the trial, this trial. As I say it could be the 6th of November 2000. I'm saying it could be, might be, in order to show that we are flexible because the definitive date will be decided, of course, depending on what the Chamber itself will decide on the 23rd of June after the hearing in respect to the amended attachment to the indictment. It's been understood that this could have an impact on the time periods depending on the decision that will be taken by that Trial Chamber in its entirety, but what we are projecting, what we've got in mind, is the opening of the trial on the 6th of November 2000, that is, as I say, this year. As regards that point, in any case, we're going to speak about that as we speak about the possible consequences of choosing that date. As regards that specific point, would you like to make any comments? The Prosecution, Ms. Hollis, or the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would not be in a position to make any informed comments about that date at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, today is June 7th and it has been exactly a year that my client has been arrested and brought before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vucicevic, I'm going to stop you right there. I'm not asking you now to take up the problems which have already taken up having to do with time periods. We'll get to that in a moment. But for now, as of this point as regards the 6th of November, does that in and of itself cause any problems to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will be ready to go on trial by November 6th. As a matter of fact, Your Honour, the Defence of Dragan Kolundzija is ready to proceed as far as tomorrow at 9 a.m..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Damir Dosen will be ready on the 6th of November for the beginning of the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. Petrovic. Let me now come to the third point which I have just mentioned and which has to do with the problem raised in a motion from the Prosecutor regarding the extension of the time limit for reviewing the pre-trial brief and the presentation of witnesses, the list of witnesses. Of course this is a motion which I have in front of me which was sent to us by the Prosecutor on the 24th of May 2000 and the name of that motion is: [In English] "Prosecution motion for extension of time to comply with the Trial Chamber order of 11 May 2000." [Interpretation]. This extension of the time that is touched on by the Prosecutor, the list of witnesses that is one thing, and the second is the review of the pre-trial brief. As regards the list of witnesses, I'll move afterwards to the arguments put forward by the Prosecutor for the extension of the time period. I'll come back to that in just a moment. As regards the list of witnesses, we have Rule 65 ter (E)(iv) which is very clear which says that the list of witnesses of the, that the Prosecutor plans to call, I'm referring to Rule 65 ter (E)(iv), which deals with the admission of the -- the method of the pre-trial Judge is presented in the Rules as follows: "It must include the name or pseudonym of each witness; a summary of facts on which each witness will testify; the points in the indictment as to which each witness will testify including specific references to counts and relevant paragraphs in the indictment, and the estimated length of time required for each witness." This is how the list of witnesses is presented in the rules. On the 11th of April this year, the Prosecutor -- well, Ms. Hollis, you sent us a list which has nothing to do with what I've just said and the name of that list is [In English] "Prosecution Witness List" [interpretation] which is merely a listing of potential witnesses. Obviously we were expecting what is provided for in the Rules. Let me remind that you -- I have issued you an order on the 24th of March and I set a deadline of 28 April and in fact, for which you explained nothing at all as to why you didn't respect it. I then issued an order, on my own initiative, on the 11th of May in which I set a time period or a deadline as the 1st of June. When you say that the Defence did not comply with the deadlines, and that's a normal thing you should, of course, respect them yourself. Everybody, therefore, must respect the deadlines under the supervision and the authority of the pre-trial Judge. Therefore, I've set a new deadline for the 1st of June, that same deadline which was set for you for presenting a pre-trial -- a revised pre-trial brief. It was then that you sent to me your request for an extension of the deadline and that was on the 11th of May. The arguments which you put forward according to which -- your team is busy with the Kvocka case and one of your legal officers is not available and these are -- at the very least surprising reasons all the more so because in the Kvocka case, we received a list of witnesses as detailed and precise as could be expected, and which completely matches the Rule. I can speak about that because I was responsible for the pre-trial management in Kvocka before I moved to another case which absolutely matches what is indicated in the Rule and which is intended to or designed to help the Chamber. And I believe that you are asking for an extension of the deadline until the 30th of September 2000. It's 30th of September. That is July, August, September that you're asking for, a three-month extension which is also very surprising, you must agree. The Kolundzija and Dosen cases are being led by the same team, and including the Kvocka case, as I just said, you could have taken some inspiration from the list that was prepared for the Kvocka case. As regards the list of witnesses, that's what I have to say. I'll get back to the deadline once I've spoken about the pre-trial brief. What I would like to know from you, Ms. Hollis, or from your team, is whether you have understood what's expected from you as regards the fact that you must respect the Rule which I've just mentioned, Rule 65 ter (E)(iv).

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, regarding your initial order that the list of witnesses be provided, the Prosecution must state that it did not understand that to be the Rule 65 ter (E)(iv) list of witnesses. The Prosecution's understanding was that a list of witnesses which was initially ordered was the list of witnesses who would either provide redacted or unredacted statements at that time. Therefore, the Prosecution submitted the list which it submitted. We certainly do understand at this point what it is you are requiring of us, what you had attempted to communicate to us although we did not understand it. And we do understand the requirements of the rule itself. We also understand the great amount of work that went into the Kvocka summary that was made involving several peoples' efforts over a considerable period of time. So we are very appreciative of the need to be very comprehensive and detailed in those summaries and we certainly do understand the requirements of the Rule. I find myself again apologising to this Chamber for a failure to comply with what has been ordered by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Hollis. Let me now move to the second aspect of this extension, which has to do with the pre-trial brief, the revised pre-trial brief. Here too, of course, we are only applying the Rules, and the Rules state, in Rule 65 ter (E)(i), that the Prosecutor must file within the deadline set by the appropriate [inaudible] which gives out the points of law and fact, which include a written presentation having to do with the nature of this case. [In English] Setting out the nature of her case. [Interpretation] Why is this? That is because when we have indictments which only list the charges which you plan to bring against the accused, I think we're going to get this quickly, a list of the witnesses with a summary of the points on which they are going to testify, and of course we'll see the relationship between those points in the testimony and the charges. The pre-trial brief comes at a point, in order to support the case, to explain what the relationship is between those materials, that is, in the evidence which you're able to collect and which allow you to support your case; that is, to support the charges which appear in the indictment. This is something which is not theoretical, but rather which has a practical effect, because it's going to allow us to know what the strategy is going to be, what are the charges you are bringing against the accused, and how you intend to argue those charges. That is the pre-trial brief which will allow us to prepare for the opening of the case. It's not a theoretical operation. What is it you've sent to us? You've sent to us -- I've got it in front of me and I've read it in its entirety -- you sent to us a pre-trial brief which is 90 pages long and in which almost everything is theoretical. I unfortunately must tell you that from 1 to 20, there's an analysis of the general situation of the camps and of what happened in the camps in question, Keraterm, et cetera, and that is in the other case as well. And then from pages 20 almost to page 62, we have part of -- well, a part which deals with the various charges and a theoretical analysis of the various Articles in the Statute -- 3, 5, et cetera -- on the violation of the laws and customs of war, on the crimes against humanity, on the Tribunal's case law in general on that subject. And then we have a long development on Article 7(1) and 7(3), which deal with the responsibility. And what's left that's concrete? Very little, except perhaps starting at page 65, a few pages which deal with the common purpose, where you provided some concrete elements dealing with the specific case. Therefore, I unfortunately must say to you, because you're saying that you didn't understand what it was that we expected from you, I'm trying to help you to understand what it is that we expect. You say, "Yes, but in this Tribunal, things are always done that way." On this point too, that's not quite true, because -- perhaps in the cases in which you were working, but there are other cases; referring to the pre-trial brief in the Kunarac case, for instance, which I have here right in front of me. And you will see that whenever there are general questions which arise in the Kunarac -- paragraph 60, for example, the general problem is said and it's put forth, and it says "in the instant case," and then it says that the accused was this and that and they were going to this and that, whether dates and giving the facts, et cetera, and the witnesses who are going to come in order to prove. And then afterwards, it says, "We're going to say the evidence will demonstrate ...", and then the evidence is specifically mentioned, the evidence which is going to be used in support of this or that situation. That's how I would like you to work. That's what I expect from you. In the Kunarac case, you also see that there's paragraph 130, where it says: "The evidence will establish ...", et cetera. In other words, each time we are brought back to the specific case, starting with the testimony and the evidence which the Prosecution has available to it. I could also refer you to a pre-trial brief from a case which I am more familiar with than others, that is, the Kordic case, the pre-trial brief dated 25 March 1999, and where you could also see there's a connection made between the purely general aspects, which recall the Tribunal's case law. And in parenthesis, I could tell you that we don't need you to recall the Tribunal's case law to us because we're familiar with it. You can simply put in references, because we are very familiar with all of that. I could even say that is our profession. We are professional Judges, and therefore we are familiar with the Tribunal's case law, and international case law in more general terms. But what we expect from you is for you to tell us how you're going to prove the guilt of the accused who are here. How, and using what method. Of course, you're going to do it during the trial, but putting forward your case, that's what it is, explaining what you're going to do and how you're going to do it. And then we're going to ask the Defence to tell us how it's going to present its defence, and that is part of the Defence pre-trial brief, which presents its case, and at that point we can start the trial under absolutely equitable conditions. We understand, of course, that the documents that we expect from you, Ms. Hollis, are additional ones. The witness summaries, which are specific, these are materials which compliment and which also allow you to draft your pre-trial draft. Both of these documents are extremely important documents which must specify the factual and legal questions having to do with this specific case. I hope that I've been clear, because you asked me to be clear. Have I been specific enough in respect of what I was just saying, because you tell me that you didn't really understand what it was that I was asking you, and now I would like to know from you whether you understood what it is that I want.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you very much. We certainly have understood the comments that you have made and what it is you want in the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Hollis. I know your position, and I also know the position of the Defence. Now we've got to discuss the issue of time periods. You told us that you were overworked at the moment, that you have problems in respect of the deadline, and you said that you didn't understand things. But now things have been cleared up, and you do understand that we cannot wait until the 30th of September. That just wouldn't be serious. At a point when, from all sides, as you know, people are saying that this Tribunal has to accelerate its procedures. It's got to try people within normal time periods, and we cannot wait until the 30th of September. I am asking you what would be the possible deadline that you would need for the presentation of these two documents, and what I suggest to you, in respect of the possible date for the trial's opening, in light of the prospects, or the prospects that I've just sketched out for you here, I was going to suggest to you mid-July, that is, the 14th of July. I would like to have your opinion on that, if you would be so kind. Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that the Prosecution can meet that deadline. And when we asked for the 30th of September, we understood how long a time that was, but we asked for it because we believe that is the time it takes. Certainly, whatever time you set for us, we will make a great effort to meet it, but I could not assure this Chamber that we could meet that deadline. And I'm being very candid at the risk of your displeasure, Your Honour, but that is my response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Do you have another proposal, aside from the 30th of September, in light of the Defence position of which you have been informed? You have been informed, haven't you, of the Defence position?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we certainly understand the Defence position. And, Your Honour, I think the only position we could give you, because the 30th of September was not a bargaining date, it was a date we felt we needed, so the only position I can give you is if Your Honour would give the Prosecution as much time as you could possibly give us. Then we will do everything that we can to meet the deadline. But the reasons I set forth for the delay are very serious reasons for us, and unfortunately, no matter how dedicated you are, there's only so much you can do within a given period of time. So I think we would have to leave it in the Chamber's hands, and certainly we'll do our mightiest to comply with whatever order you give us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The proposal which I'm going to make in order to take into account both the Defence's concerns and the Prosecutor's, the proposal that I am going to make is that the pre-trial brief, the revised one, and the list of witnesses, in compliance with Rule 65 ter, must be filed by the 28th of July, that is, before recess, before the legal recess which is scheduled for the month of August. That's the proposal which I'm making. Would you like to speak, Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I sympathise with the problems that the Office of the Prosecutor has in addressing the difficulties in answering to the Court's orders. However, Your Honour, I am fully aware that not a single party to these proceedings will ever be 100 per cent ready. I understand the diligence and expectation that Ms. Hollis has of herself and her own team, but the higher expectation we put, sometimes we can never reach them. We have to work in terms of practicalities, and indeed the Statute and the Rules do not provide any time for the Prosecution to get ready. This is not, I believe, the matter of equality of arms, because a year ago when my client was arrested, the Prosecution should have been ready to try the case. I do thank you for being candid in understanding that the judicial schedule is such that this case cannot be taken up before November 6th. However, Your Honour, I would like you to take these two dates under advisement, depending on the Trial Chamber's ruling on the 23rd of June based on our motions for bifurcated trial, because if the Trial Chamber accepts -- grants that motion, the amount of work that Ms. Hollis and her team will have to do will be, indeed, bifurcated and may be cut by four times than it would be necessary, and depending -- maybe perhaps if I could suggest that they could get a shorter schedule to present the statement of the witnesses and then a little bit longer date to present a trial brief. Therefore, they would be a lot more accommodating to you pending our motion for a bifurcated trial. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're speaking about the motion having to do with separation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I hold to what I've already said. Certain adaptations are possible, of course, depending on what the Chamber decides on the 23rd of June, but I would like to hold to my decision for the time being, which will be put into a scheduling order and will be issued after this Status Conference, which is to ask the Prosecutor, as a deadline, to provide to the Chamber, to the Pre-Trial Judge, the list of witnesses in accordance with Rule 65 ter as I have recalled, and the revised pre-trial brief for the 28th of July, which will allow us, of course, to review the document before the court recess. Mr. Vucicevic, in light of this decision of the 28th of July, I know that you submitted a motion, an alternative one in which you say that should that date of the 30th of September be granted, you're asking for provisional release of your client, that is, Mr. Kolundzija. In light of the new date, that is, the 28th of July, are you going to maintain that request or are you going to withdraw it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to withdraw that, and I do thank you for being so considerate to our concerns. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Vucicevic. The request for provisional release has now been withdrawn by Mr. Vucicevic. The last point -- the last substantive point that I would like to deal with with you in this Status Conference has to do with the question of the other time limits which we need in order to prepare the trial and to start the trial around the 6th of November. First of all, there is a whole set of documents which must be presented, according to Rule 65 ter (E), which are connected to discussions between the parties. I received, before coming to this conference, to this hearing, I received from you a document which is called [In English] "Regarding Admissions by Parties and Points of Agreement and Disagreements on Matters of Fact and Law," [Interpretation] which is dated 7 June and which follows up on a meeting that I asked for. I asked for this in an order which was not completely respected. It was on the 31st of March. I asked you for six weeks, and you only met on the 5th of June, without having asked for any extension of the time period. I'm just saying this in passing. You met on the 5th of June, as planned, and you sent to us a document which mentions the points of agreement and disagreement between you. That is the points which are in dispute -- excuse me, rather on facts of law and fact. It also says in Rule 65 ter (E) that there must be a pre-trial brief addressing the factual and legal issues, a statement of contested matters of fact and law, and a list of exhibits the Prosecutor intends to offer, stating where possible where the Defence has any objection to its authenticity. That is, the presentation of the list by the Prosecutor and any possible objection as to the authenticity by the Defence. The list of exhibits was submitted on the 28th of April. Do the parties have any comments in respect of their progress and -- about the meeting which you had on the 5th of June. Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, we did meet on the 5th of June. The Defence had asked for extensions for various filings and had been involved in investigations, so we met on the 5th of June. We discussed a variety of issues, including all of the motions that are outstanding before the Chamber. We also discussed the elements that are set forth in the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, and we determined at that meeting that there are no admissions at this point. And at that meeting, after discussions, we were only able to come to agreement on the points that have been listed in the report. The Defence for both accused have agreed to various of the adjudicated facts, and you have been provided with a document showing the facts which each accused has agreed to. Aside from that agreement, Your Honour, the only other agreement that we reached was an agreement involving the time period for the disclosure to the Defence of the names of protected witnesses. And as noted in the report, Defence counsel for accused Kolundzija explained the reasons why he wished to have those names 60 days before the trial. After hearing those reasons, the Prosecutor agreed that that would be a reasonable period of time, and subject to the pre-trial Judge's approval or the Trial Chamber's approval, if necessary, we would be prepared to provide those names to both counsel 60 days before the commencement of trial. But aside from those agreements, no other agreements were reached on any matters of fact or any matter of law. Therefore, as of today, every other issue remains in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Hollis. Would the Defence like to make any comment about the meeting which was held on the 5th of June? Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the meeting was very cordial and very businesslike, and I am looking forward to more meetings of this kind if we are going to solve any outstanding issues that we can have some common ground on. I fully concur with the statements that Ms. Hollis has made to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to say that I agree with what my learned friends have just said and to say that the accused Dosen's Defence has accepted what was said today. But whether -- in case of the disclosure of the material, it will also depend on the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution, which we are expecting with impatience. We hope that we shall be able to make bigger progress and there will be many more things that we will be able to agree about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. Petrovic. At least in so far as you are concerned, I do want to encourage you to try as many points of convergence as possible in order to avoid any further delays in the conduct of the trial. I therefore take notice for the protected witnesses, the names will be communicated 60 days beforehand. As for the judicial notice, I also take note of the list upon which you have reached the agreement. As regards the motions, there are still those that have to do with the admission of documents. Do you want to present any additional comments having to do with admission of documents before the 23rd of June, before the conference of the 23rd of June? Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. What about the Defence? No? Well, at any rate, you will have the possibility to raise these points at the meeting of the 23rd of June, at the conference at the 23rd of June, as you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... no arguments then, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right then on those points it will be the 23rd of June. Another point which is the consequence of what has just been said, I would like to set also a time, a deadline for the filing of the Defence pre-trial brief, and I was thinking about the middle of September. I would like to know whether the Defence could present its pre-trial brief as provided for in the Rules now. Would the Defence be in a position to present its brief? It could be the 11th of September but it could also be the end of that week, that is the 14th of September. I'd like to know whether the Defence, in light of the fact that the Prosecution is going to file its brief on the 28th of July, could the Defence file its brief in the middle of September? Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could kindly ask you if you can give us a deadline the first week in October because I am planning to take another investigative trip in August, and I would like to take some time before that for vacation. Since I am the only working on the case and it's been a year, very arduous work, and still -- I believe we will have a full month for -- to have a Pre-Trial Conference so if you could set a deadline the first week, I would appreciate it because I am thinking of coming back in the second week of September, coming back from Bosnia. So then it would give me very little office time to comply with that, Your Honour. But whatever you say, Your Honour, I will change my schedule and I will try to accommodate your orders. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had planned to set the date for the first half -- that is around the 11th of October. I'm speaking about the date for the pre-trial conference. Excuse me, Mr. Petrovic, did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. All I wanted to say is that Mr. Dosen's Defence can prepare the pre-trial brief by the date that you suggested, that is, the 14th of September is, at this point in time, quite acceptable to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In order to accommodate both Defence counsel, could we set the date for the 30th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we're going to set the date for the filing of the Defence pre-trial brief at the 30th of September. At that point, and of course these are dates which will be -- which will be set. But as I've already told you, they are subject to any decision the Trial Chamber might take during the meeting of the 23rd of June which might change those dates, depending on what the decision of the Trial Chamber is going to be as regards the attached indictment. At that point, the Pre-Trial Conference could take place on the 11th of October. As regards preparing for the trial, I plan to organise a Status Conference in order to see the status of all the preparations and that will be around the middle of September and the suggested date is September 13th. That would be the date for the next Status Conference whose purpose is to see where things stand in respect of the status. A final question, Ms. Hollis, which you, yourself, mentioned, I believe, is to ask you where you stand in respect of deposition proceedings. If I remember correctly, you told the Chamber that there was the possibility that some of the witnesses would be common ones with the Kvocka case, and that we could use deposition evidence. Do you have anything else that you want to tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We still have the same, I believe it's in the form of a motion that is outstanding regarding ways to either have concurrent presentation of the same evidence or perhaps to have that evidence be introduced in this trial and we haven't changed our position on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. All right. I'd like you to go into more depth, in that as far as that question is concerned, if you have any concrete proposals that you want to make to us which would allow us to move the trial forward in the interests of justice, those suggestions would be most welcome. I think that I have covered all the questions I wanted to speak about with you today during this Status Conference. Now, if you have any other questions you'd like to raise that I didn't think about, of course this is the time to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Kolundzija's Defence has no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, nothing in particular at the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In the case if there are any questions you can think about, you don't have to worry, because on the 23rd of June, that is soon, you will have an opportunity to ask them in front of the full Chamber. I would like in accordance with Rule 65 bis (A)(ii) to ask about the mental and physical condition of the accused. Mr. Kolundzija and Mr. Dosen, it's being understood that the accused of course can -- I'm sorry I have to speak a moment with the senior trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We understand that if the accused want to say anything in closed session to the Chamber, since this is a public session, all they have to do is to tell us and we'll move into a closed session and then there will be discussions in private. Let me remind you also that according to the Rules, if the accused have any problems they must first speak to the commander and then to speak to the Registry, but they can speak directly with the Trial Chamber, and this is an occasion or an opportunity which is provided for in this status conference, that's either through yourselves or through your counsel, if you have anything to say about the -- your mental or physical condition, we are of course prepared to hear them. This has to do with the detention conditions. Mr. Dosen. THE ACCUSED DOSEN: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no. I have no complaints except that I've never been locked up before so I do not know what a prison is like, but for the time being, everything is all right. I have no particular complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No, we were not inviting criticisms. It was simply if you felt any problems regarding your detention. I gather that you do not have any particular problems at the moment. Mr. Kolundzija, how about you? THE ACCUSED KOLUNDZIJA: [Interpretation] Everything is in perfect order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you, so let me remind you that after this, the result of the Status Conference, there will be an order that will be indicated to you with the time limits which have been set up with you in your presence and I should equally like to remind you that on the 23rd of June, depending on the agenda which I have communicated to you, there will again be a hearing with the Chamber sitting in full. This session is adjourned, thank you. -- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 6.10 p.m. 23 24 25
